title: Geometrically complex microfluidic devices for the study of cell migration
protocol: Design photomask in Coreldraw X18 or Autocad.
Convert file to Gerber format using Linkcad.
Order class 4 photomask, 5” square quartz, 1µ resolution from JD Photo data.
Take a 4” wafer and bake at 110°C for 5 min. to remove water.
Spin coat SU-8 2005 at 3000 RPM for 5µm high structures.
Soft bake on hotplate at 95°C for 2 min.
Expose 90 – 105 mJ/cm2 on the EVG mask aligner.
Post exposure bake 95°C for 3 min.
Develop SU-8 in SU-8 Developer.
Place the wafers in a wafer carrier.
Pipette 20µl of silane into the falcon tube and eject the tip into it.
Apply vacuum on the dessicator, at least 0.1 bar.
Seal the desiccator and turn off the vacuum pump to allow the silane to vaporize.
Wait 1h in the sealed desiccator.
Vent the desiccator after 1 hour.
Dispose silane as hazardous waste.
Wafers are now hydrophobic and coated with a monolayer of silane.
Make a 6”x6” square of aluminum foil.
Shape aluminium foil around the wafer to make a circular tray.
Place the wafer inside the tray.
Place the tray inside a square petri dish.
Pour approximately 50g of PDMS (10:1 ratio) into a Thinky mixer cup.
Mix the PDMS in the Thinky mixer at 2000 RPM for 2 minutes.
Defoam the mixed PDMS at 2000 RPM for 2 minutes.
Pour the mixed PDMS onto the wafer.
Place the wafer and dish inside a vacuum desiccator.
Pump out remaining bubbles using a vacuum pump.
Vent as necessary to pop the bubbles.
Cover the petri dish with its lid.
Place the covered dish in an oven at 80°C overnight.
Cut off all PDMS and foil from the back of the wafer using a razor blade.
Peel off the PDMS carefully, keeping features facing upward.
Avoid touching the surface during peeling.
Cut the PDMS into small pieces according to design specifications.
Punch holes in the PDMS with a 2mm Harris Unicore biopsy punch.
Alternatively, use a 12 gauge blunt sharpened needle for punching holes.
Clean the PDMS with scotch tape.
Place PDMS devices into a beaker containing 70% ethanol.
Sonicate the beaker with the PDMS devices for 5 minutes.
Devices are now ready to be plasma cleaned.
Setup a hotplate at approximately 85°C.
Dry the PDMS thoroughly with an airgun, ensuring all traces of ethanol are removed.
Place the PDMS features face up along with #1.5 glass cover slips in the plasma cleaner.
Start the vacuum pump and pump down until the plasma appears on high power for 2 minutes.
Turn off the equipment and remove the glass and PDMS from the plasma machine.
Place cover slips on hot plate.
Press PDMS, features facing downward, onto cover slip slightly for bonding.
Wait 2 hours with bonded devices at 85°C.
For additional bonding, place bonded devices in oven overnight at 80°C.
Glue cover slip bound PDMS device to Petri dish with hole using aquarium glue.
Let the glue harden overnight.
Place dish with glued PDMS device into plasma cleaner.
Remove lid of the dish and apply vacuum for 2 minutes.
Switch on plasma cleaner to high for another 2 minutes.
Pipette ~3 ml of warm R10 onto the PDMS device.
Flush the device through the punched holes, ensuring no air bubbles inside.
Incubate in a humidified incubator at 37°C/5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Remove medium from the top of the PDMS device to prevent mixing on top.
Designate one hole for chemokine and another for cells.
Carefully remove 5 μl of medium from the cell hole.
Remove 10 μl from the chemokine hole and replace with chemokine.
Pipette 5 μl of cell suspension (50,000 cells) into the cell hole carefully.
Put back into incubator; cells will start to migrate after 2-3 hours.
Start imaging at microscope of choice.
